first: A fixed, eye-height wide diagonal view from the rear customer-side corner of a modest working bakery toward its front wall: cream plaster, honey-coloured timber, worn stone flooring, and dark metal baking equipment, with clean but comfortably used surfaces. The blue glazed front door is far left, its shop-name sign mounted at adult chest height; the large clear front window is far right. The wooden shop counter occupies middle left and runs from near to far. Against the right wall, the closed baking oven is middle right, the empty wire cooling rack is near right, and the wooden workbench is far right with its working edge toward the camera; one flour bowl rests at the far-right end of its worktop. Baker stands at the oven facing it, wearing the two thick cream quilted oven mitts, with neither hand holding anything. One loaf and one pastry tray containing six croissants are inside the closed oven and not yet visible. The workbench has no tray on it, and the window is at its initial brightness.
